facts: Antarctica is a desert: its interior receives very little precipitation.
Antarctica holds roughly 70% of Earth's freshwater reserves, locked in ice.
Antarctica's ice sheet averages nearly two kilometres thick.
The lowest directly measured air temperature was recorded at Antarctica's Vostok Station: −89.2°C.
Antarctica was once part of Gondwana and supported forests.
Antarctica has rivers, including a seasonal meltwater river called the Onyx.
Lake Vostok lies hidden beneath Antarctica's ice sheet.
Antarctica's Mount Erebus is an active volcano near the South Pole.
Antarctica is almost twice the size of Australia.
The Antarctic Treaty prohibits nuclear explosions and radioactive-waste disposal on the continent.
The Sahara is the largest hot desert, but the polar deserts are larger.
The Sahara spans roughly a third of Africa.
The Sahara has repeatedly shifted between dry desert and much greener landscapes.
The Sahara's highest mountain, Emi Koussi, is a volcano.
The Sahara includes rocky plateaus and gravel plains, not just sand dunes.
Some Saharan dunes rise more than 180 metres high.
The name Sahara comes from an Arabic word for deserts.
The Sahel forms a semi-arid transition between the Sahara and wetter regions farther south.
The Sahara reaches from the Atlantic Ocean to the Red Sea.
The Sahara contains entire mountain ranges, including the Tibesti and Ahaggar.
Lake Baikal holds more freshwater than all five North American Great Lakes combined.
Lake Baikal reaches more than 1.6 kilometres deep.
At around 25–30 million years old, Baikal is Earth's oldest surviving lake.
Lake Baikal occupies a rift where Earth's crust is slowly pulling apart.
Lake Baikal's surface is above sea level, but its deepest bottom lies far below it.
Lake Baikal is slightly larger in surface area than Belgium.
Lake Baikal has islands; the largest, Olkhon, is about 72 kilometres long.
The Angara is the river through which Lake Baikal drains.
Many species living in Lake Baikal occur nowhere else.
Kilometres of sediment beneath Lake Baikal preserve a long record of changing climates.
The Dead Sea is actually a landlocked lake, not a sea.
The Dead Sea's shores form Earth's lowest exposed land.
The Dead Sea is roughly ten times saltier than the ocean.
The Dead Sea's dense, salty water makes people unusually buoyant.
The Jordan River feeds the Dead Sea, but no river flows out.
The Dead Sea supplied asphalt used in ancient Egyptian mummification.
The Dead Sea has shrunk dramatically as water that once fed it has been diverted.
The Dead Sea is very salty, but some other lakes and ponds are saltier.
The Dead Sea lies between Jordan, the West Bank and Israel.
The Dead Sea's Hebrew name means Sea of Salt.
